evals.prompt: We're a product team with EKS already running non-AI workloads, and we want to self-host an open LLM (Llama 3 8B class) for a product feature. Target ~100-500ms TTFT, balanced cost posture, no strong hardware preference. Lay out the full GenAI-on-EKS stack: hardware, scheduler, serving framework, storage, observability, and the gateway, plus a 30/60/90 build path.
expectations: Recommends NVIDIA GPU (g6 or g6e) as the time-to-value default.
Explicitly flags AWS Neuron / Inferentia2 as a phase-2 cost-optimization option rather than reflexively picking GPU only.
Specifies Karpenter as the autoscaler.
Specifies the NVIDIA device plugin.
Specifies an EKS-optimized accelerated AMI (Bottlerocket/AL2023).
Recommends vLLM as the inference engine (optionally fronted by Ray Serve for autoscaling).
Recommends that vLLM expose an OpenAI-compatible API.
Covers model-weight storage via Mountpoint for S3 CSI.
Covers observability via DCGM Exporter + Prometheus/Grafana.
Covers observability including a token-latency (TTFT) metric.
Includes the security baseline: EKS Pod Identity/IRSA for pod credentials (never static keys).
Recommends an AI gateway in front of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: LiteLLM as the default, or Envoy AI Gateway where L7 routing at ingress is the need.

evals.prompt: We need to fine-tune a 70B Transformer model on Amazon EKS, distributed across multiple nodes. We're cost-first, with an existing PyTorch + Hugging Face stack. Should we use GPU or Neuron? How do we handle EFA networking, checkpointing, and Spot safely?
expectations: Recommends AWS Neuron (Trn2/Trn1) as the cost-leader for Transformer-family training.
Recommends NVIDIA p5/H100 as the fallback.
Mentions EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML for guaranteed capacity.
Specifies Karpenter for Neuron compute.
Specifies the Neuron device plugin for Neuron compute.
States that the Neuron DRA driver (Kubernetes 1.34 and later) is not supported on EKS Auto Mode, so Neuron nodes on Auto Mode use the Neuron device plugin.
Names the NVIDIA device plugin, or the NVIDIA DRA driver on Kubernetes 1.34 and later, as the compute device manager on the GPU path.
Specifies the EFA device plugin as a networking complement on the GPU path for multi-node NCCL/MPI.
Specifies the EFA device plugin as a networking complement on the Neuron path for multi-node NCCL/MPI.
Calls out EFA networking with NUMA pinning (single-numa-node) for multi-node training.
Calls out the static CPU manager for multi-node training.
Calls out NCCL/MPI in the container image for multi-node training.
Recommends FSx for Lustre in the same AZ as the compute nodes.
Recommends an S3 Data Repository Association for durable checkpoint offload.
States that Spot is acceptable for training only with checkpoint/resume logic.
Includes Pod Identity in the security baseline.
Includes private subnets in the security baseline.
